overview.title: AI-Factory v2.1
overview.badge: AI Company Platform · Single Docker Stack
overview.intro: Production-grade stack in one container (FastAPI + Next.js).
overview.introAutonomousSuffix: mode feeds market research and generated ideas;
overview.introOnDemandSuffix: mode starts from the customer's phrase — same stages, same QA gates.
overview.introEnd: Typical deliverables are share-ready landings; crypto checkout and sandbox preview ship with the bundle.
capabilities: Specialized pipeline roles in the admin roster: Analyst, PM, Methodologist, Architect, Designer (UX), Developer, QA, Security, DevOps, Marketing, Sales, Evolution Analyst — plus Director as a meta-agent. `agents/` in the repo is the source of truth; `ui_experience` in architecture is the binding UX brief for the Developer.
Multi-LLM routing with failover — local Ollama, DeepSeek, Together, Groq
Director AI — scheduled analysis, decisions queue, reports
Crypto storefront — USDT/USDC (Base, Arbitrum, Ethereum, Solana); default list ~$4.99 USDT when sales artifacts omit price
Glass storefront & admin — animations, responsive layout
Enterprise-minded ops — secrets paths, audit hooks, sandbox isolation
CLI companion for operators (`ai-company` where installed)
overview.singleContainerBody: Everything runs in one Docker container (Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.12, Node.js 20). No external dependencies required.

ownerGuide.badge: Operator scenarios · Storefront policy · Support vs pipeline
ownerGuide.intro: This section is for the person running a deployed instance: provisioning LLMs, watching the pipeline, curating the marketplace, and helping buyers. Deep tab reference lives in docs/admin-guide.md; REST patterns in docs/api-integration-guide.md.
firstDayItems: Confirm a host bind mount for /app/data (see root README — avoid anonymous Docker volumes).
Sign in at /admin/login and rotate the admin password; enable TOTP if desired.
Open LLM Providers — wire at least one model backend and verify routing rules.
Submit an idea from New Product or run CLI discover / create-idea inside the container.
Watch Pipeline — expand a card, click stage tiles for task payloads and errors.
Optional: run README full_pipeline_smoke.py against a completed product ID.
marketplaceItems: Locate a COMPLETED row → Storefront panel.
Edit Marketplace copy to tune card/detail text (persisted to marketing_content.json).
If automatic quality gates block listing but you accept the risk: Force public storefront + justification.
To pull a SKU offline: Not pursuing (with reason) or Hide from public storefront — shoppers lose listing + detail 404.
Remember: Dashboard “Completed” counts lifecycle; storefront visibility adds code + quality + hide rules.

architecture.intro: AI-Factory follows a modular architecture with clear separation of concerns. All components run inside a single Docker container, communicating via internal HTTP and the filesystem.
architecture.requestFlowBody: User requests go to Next.js on port 8080. API calls to /api/* are proxied by Next.js rewrites to the FastAPI backend on port 8081. The admin panel is served by Next.js as well.

quickstart.intro: Deploy and run the AI-Factory platform with a single Docker command.
quickstart.loginIntro: There is no default admin123 password. On first startup with an empty data volume, the entrypoint asks for a password in the console when stdin is a TTY; otherwise it writes a one-time password to data/secrets/bootstrap_admin.txt. See docs/security.md in the repository.
loginItems: Password: set at first bootstrap (console prompt or bootstrap file)
quickstart.dockerSandboxBody: The factory image can run isolated preview containers (network none, dropped capabilities). Host-gateway to reach Ollama on the host is opt-in via docker-compose.host-gateway.yml — not enabled by default.

adminPanel.intro: The admin panel at /admin provides complete control over the AI-Factory platform. It is protected by JWT-based authentication with optional 2FA (TOTP).
authItems: Brute-force protection: max 5 failed attempts per 15 minutes
dashboardItems: Pipeline metrics — total/active/completed/failed products, pending/running/timed-out tasks
Resource usage — CPU, memory, disk utilization
Product P&L — live per-product unit economics: revenue vs. LLM cost, gross margin, ROI and cost-recovery
Security status — system health indicator, recent failed logins
providersItems: View all configured providers with status (online/offline/degraded)
Configure routing rules per task type
agentsItems: View status of all 11 pipeline roles (including Designer)
Configure timeouts, retry limits, and priorities
securityItems: View audit logs with date/action/user filters
directorItems: View latest Director reports with metrics and recommendations
settingsItems: Choose from 5 themes: Cyberpunk, Minimal, Glass, Neon, Corporate
Theme applies dynamically without page reload

agents.intro: The platform uses ten core agents plus a Methodologist gate and the Evolution Analyst meta-agent, each with a strict role. Director AI sits above the loop. Agents communicate through the filesystem — no agent can modify another agent's work. For web deliverables, the Architect also emits ui_experience (tokens, typography, motion) so the Developer ships intentional UI — shown as a dedicated
agents.introSuffix: step on the public pipeline diagram.

safetyItems: Strict role boundaries — no agent can perform another agent's tasks
Timeout protection — agents have 30-second execution limit (configurable)
Output validation — all agent outputs are validated against schemas
Escalation — if an agent fails repeatedly, the Director AI is notified
Filesystem-based memory — no context hallucination, all state is on disk

pipeline.intro: The product lifecycle follows a deterministic state machine with 13 states. Each state is handled by a specific agent, ensuring clear ownership and accountability.
pipeline.introOnDemand: Autonomous products still consume analyst/marketing idea flows; on-demand products anchor every downstream agent on the customer brief — not a separate lightweight conveyor for orders.
featuresItems: Deterministic FSM — each product follows the same state machine
Error recovery — if QA finds bugs, product loops back to DEV_FIXING
Timeout management — each step has a configurable timeout (default 30s)
Parallel execution — multiple products can be in different pipeline stages
State persistence — JSON (default) or optional SQLite3 backend with CLI migration
Director override — Director AI can adjust timeouts and priorities
Per-product LLM spend cap (USD) — set in Admin → Settings → Pipeline & product quality (0 = unlimited); optional env AIFACTORY_MAX_PIPELINE_COST_USD overrides
Pipeline product cards show inline charts: LLM spend by agent, timeline progress, quality score
pipeline.directorCycleIntro: In parallel with the product pipeline, the Director AI runs every 4 hours:
directorCycleItems: 1. Collect metrics from all sources (state files, telemetry, logs, database)
2. Analyze metrics against target values, identify anomalies and trends
3. Generate decisions — auto-apply allowed actions, queue recommendations for admin
5. Notify admin panel with ready report

crypto.intro: AI-Factory supports multi-chain crypto payments for generated products. Customers can purchase products using USDT or USDC stablecoins.
crypto.economicsBody: Storefront and checkout default to about $4.99 USDT when marketing/sales files do not specify another price — tuned for impulse landing purchases while operators override per SKU.
paymentFlowItems: Customer selects product and chooses a network (Base/Solana/Arbitrum)
System generates a unique payment address and amount
Customer sends USDT/USDC to the provided address
On sufficient confirmations — product license is activated
Customer gains access to sandbox demo and full product
crypto.walletBody: Platform wallets are configured via the CLI. Wallet addresses are displayed in the admin panel under Crypto Settings. Withdrawals require multi-signature approval.

uniCredit.intro: UNI is internal store credit pegged to USDT — not a tradable token. All in-platform debits and credits use whole UNI at a fixed rate; USDT is only the on-ramp and off-ramp through platform treasury wallets.
uniCredit.pegBody: 1 UNI = $0.01 USDT (100 UNI per $1). This supports micro-billing for LLM calls without floating-point USDT ledgers. Configure via AIFACTORY_UNI_USD_CENTS_PER_UNI=1 (legacy alias AIFACTORY_UNI_USDT_RATE=100).
feesItems: Per invoke / channel spend: 5% platform fee (AIFACTORY_UNI_PLATFORM_FEE_BPS=500)
Platform fees accrue to wallet owner_id=PLATFORM_FEES — withdrawn like any seller
uniCredit.treasuryBody: On-chain USDT in treasury must cover all outstanding user UNI at the peg. Background job uni_treasury_audit records reserve_ratio; alert when below 0.999. Set AIFACTORY_UNI_TREASURY_USDT_OBSERVED for manual audits until chain indexer is wired.
flowItems: Customer tops up USDT → POST /api/uni/topup/confirm → UNI credited (receipt kind=topup)
AI Market channel open → hold reserves UNI; invoke → spend_hold splits 95% seller / 5% platform
Direct capability purchase → charge() atomically debits buyer and credits seller + platform
Seller withdraw → POST /api/uni/withdraw → queued on-chain payout (dispatcher integration)
uniCredit.settingsBody: Pipeline per-product LLM cap (USD) lives under Admin → Settings → Pipeline & product quality → Max LLM cost per product (quality.max_pipeline_cost_usd). UNI economics do not replace this cap — they complement on-chain commerce.
uniCredit.docsMarkdown: See also docs/uni-economics.md and docs/postgres-production-runbook.md in the repository.

security.intro: AI-Factory implements enterprise-grade security measures across all layers.
authItems: Brute-force protection: 5 failed attempts max per 15 minutes
All admin actions logged to tamper-evident audit log
sandboxItems: Filesystem isolation — no access to host files
dataProtectionItems: Secrets encrypted at rest using Fernet (symmetric encryption)
Audit logs are append-only with tamper detection
Rate limiting on all API endpoints
No sensitive data returned in API responses
monitoringItems: Real-time security dashboard in admin panel
Failed login attempt tracking with IP logging
Audit log export in JSON format
security.firstPasswordBodyPrefix: No fixed default password. Use the console prompt on first TTY start, read
security.firstPasswordBodySuffix: for detached Compose, or rotate via Admin → Users. CSRF protection applies to cookie-based admin sessions (X-CSRF-Token header).

director.intro: The Director AI is a meta-agent that oversees the entire platform. It does not participate in product development but evaluates system performance and makes optimization decisions.
cycleItems: 1. Metrics Collection — gathers data from pipeline state, telemetry, logs, and financial records
2. Analysis — compares metrics against targets, identifies anomalies and trends
3. Decision Making — generates automatic actions (if enabled) and recommendations
4. Report Generation — creates detailed markdown report
5. Notification — updates admin panel with new report
director.autoActionsIntro: When enabled, the Director AI can automatically:
autoActionsItems: Increase agent timeouts if timeout rate exceeds 15%
Trigger marketing reviews if conversion drops below 8%
Recommend switching to local models if GPU is underutilized
Adjust resource limits based on usage patterns
director.reportFormatIntro: Director reports are saved as Markdown files in /data/reports/director/ and displayed in the admin panel. Each report includes:

configuration.intro: The platform is configured through YAML and JSON files in /data/config/. Changes can be made via the admin panel or directly by editing these files.
qualityBlockItems: max_pipeline_repair_rounds — QA repair loop budget before FAILED
max_pipeline_cost_usd — per-product LLM spend cap in USD (0 = unlimited); shown on Pipeline product vitals charts
demo / visual / browser / marketplace gates — same fields as Admin → Settings → Pipeline & product quality
Env vars AIFACTORY_* override saved YAML when set (Docker hard override)
themeItems: Cyberpunk — neon cyan, purple accents, dark gradient background
Minimal — clean white/gray with subtle shadows
Glass — transparent panels with heavy blur effects
Neon — bright neon colors on dark background
